headline: Network toxicology and multi-omics nominate candidate toxicant targets and biomarkers
label: Network Toxicology Multi Omics Biomarkers
summary: Network toxicology and ML pipelines now pair multi-omics with experimental validation to nominate candidate targets for exposures and disease.
synthesis: Most items in this set apply network toxicology, multi-omics profiling, or machine learning to nominate molecular targets for environmental toxicants and disease states. Examples include ISG20 for patulin in colorectal cancer, CXCL1 and COL4A4 for cyclophosphamide-induced premature ovarian insufficiency, and NFKB1 and IL6 for trimethyltin chloride-induced epilepsy. Several toxicant studies focus on PFAS compounds, including 6:2 Cl-PFESA in non-obstructive azoospermia, PFDA in granulosa cells, and PFOS precursor effects on HepaRG lipidomics, alongside 6PPD-quinone in steatotic liver disease and bisphenol A acting through ITGAX in prostatitis. Disease-oriented work applies machine learning to phenylalanine metabolism in pancreatic cancer and to MC-LR-associated hepatocellular carcinoma. Validation is largely performed in cell lines or animal models, and the patulin candidate ISG20 is explicitly described as preliminary. The shared contribution is the coupling of computational prioritization with targeted experimental follow-up.
